input.quote: Kubient hereby grants to Customer a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable license to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient, for the purpose of serving Inventory at Target Demand
input.rationale: The only grant to us is § 2 (p0002), and it fails both fallback elements. "Customer" is defined as The Associated Press alone (p0000), the grant names no affiliates and gives no mechanism to add them, and § 6(a) affirmatively bars transfer or third-party access without Kubient's prior written approval, so there is no path for AP affiliates or contractors to use the Auction Platform. The licence is also expressly "non-transferable, non-assignable", which as the specific licence term overrides the general assignment permission in § 14(h) (p0072) and leaves the licence stranded if AP merges or sells the relevant business. Our fallback edit extends the grant to affiliates on written notice and makes it transferable to an M&A successor without Kubient's approval. We note but do not press the residual "revocable" characterisation (and the effects-of-termination revocation in p0021, which mis-cites "section 3"), as irrevocability sits only at the preferred level.

mappings.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.

proposal.summary: Extend the Auction Platform licence to AP's affiliates on written notice and make it transferable to an M&A successor.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The grant runs to AP alone and is expressly non-transferable and non-assignable, so our affiliates have no path to use the Auction Platform and the licence would not follow AP into a merger or sale. We have extended the grant to affiliates upon written notice to Kubient and made it transferable to an M&A successor, which is our fallback position.
